FALL_LOWER.narrative: An employee was picking up debris from the roof of a building. She lifted one of the skylight covers, which was not labeled "hole," and fell through 10 feet. She fractured her right arm and was hospitalized.
An employee was working on a plank supported by two A-frame ladders when the plank broke, causing the employee to fall approximately 5 feet and break the right femur. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee fell backward while removing a manhole cover, landing on the pavement and suffering a broken pelvis.

Employee #1 was helping to install a slate roof on an existing residence when he fell approximately 20 feet onto a brick porch. The extent of Employee #1’s injuries were not specified in the original report.
On March 15, 2017, Employee #1 fell from an elevation and died.

On December 29, 2010, an employee was working as a mason on a scaffold that was approximately 35 feet high, approximately 100 feet long, and equipped with weather protection. The employee was crushed when the scaffold overturned during high winds. No other details were provided in the original narrative.

FALL_SAME.narrative: An employee tripped and fell down a flight of stairs while engaged in construction operations. The employee sustained a mild concussion and was subsequently hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was supervising a concrete pouring crew. He turned to check on another crew and fell, sustaining tibia and fibula fractures that required surgery.
An employee stepped on mud while exiting a shipping container and fell backwards, suffering a concussion and possible injuries to the neck and back. The employee was hospitalized.

On October 30, 2012, Employee #1, of Rainbow Valley Design & Construction, Inc., was doing construction work at a single family dwelling. He was installing trim around a ceiling opening of a newly installed skylight fixture. He was working from a 4-foot ladder. He apparently stepped off the ladder, tripped, and hit his head on a wood stove near the work area. He was transported to River Bend Hospital for treatment of a head injury. He died at the hospital as a result of this injury. The investigation concluded that, because Employee #1 was 6 feet tall and working in an area that measured 91 inches from the floor, he could not have been more than one or two steps up the ladder when he fell.

STRUCK_BY.narrative: An employee was performing excavation work to expose a 12-foot water pipe. A large clod of dirt estimated to be 3 to 4 feet in size dislodged from a spoil pile and fell, striking his right leg. The impact caused the employee to lose consciousness momentarily. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured tibia and fibula and required surgery.

An employee was on a manlift approximately 5 feet above the ground while adjusting the rigging on a 12-foot granite column weighing approximately 12,000 pounds. The rigging failed and the column struck the manlift, causing a crush injury to the employee’s leg.
A stack of 12 x 4 foot panels of sheet rock in the hallway of an under construction building fell on the employee and broke his leg.

On June 11, 2013, Employee #1 was standing behind a coworker that was on a ladder using a reciprocating saw. After the sawing was finished, the coworker quickly lowered the saw which slung back and struck Employee #1 in the chest puncturing his heart. The employee was taken an area hospital, where he died on June 23, 2013.

At 10:40 a.m. on September 15, 2018, an employee was repairing a lawn mower. During work, the hammer that the employee was using broke and struck his right leg. The incident resulted in an injury that required surgery. Following the procedure, the employee suffered a blood clot and died as a result.

On April 24, 2013, Employee #1 was standing near a storage area, where bundles of concrete form boards are stored. The stack of four bundles tipped over and struck the employee and pinned him on the ground. Employee #1 was taken to an area hospital, where he was treated for head trauma. Employee #1 remained hospitalized.

STRUCK_AGAINST.narrative: An employee was hospitalized for possible infection of lacerations on the left arm that the employee received while attempting to remove debris from an insulation blower.

An employee was installing a 6-inch PVC sewer line. As he was holding the pipe, something smashed his thumb against the pipe. He suffered left thumb trauma and a possible fracture, requiring overnight hospitalization.
An employee was working in a shallow trench preparing to install fiberoptic cable. When he stood up, he hit his head on the bucket of a trackhoe and had a seizure.
On March 3, 2011, an employee of a plumbing, heating, and air conditioning contractor struck his head on a storage bin. He sustained a laceration, and he died.

CAUGHT.narrative: An employee was moving concrete panels when his left index finger was pinched between a panel and a piece of wood. The finger was partially amputated.

An employee was in a scissor lift welding a clip angle and needed to reposition the scissor lift for the next weld. While repositioning the scissor lift, his left hand was caught between the top rail and an existing pipe support, resulting in a partial pinky fingertip amputation.
An employee was cutting decking with a handheld saw when the saw cut his leg.

On October 29, 2011, Employee #1 was at a two-story commercial structure that was undergoing renovation. The first floor support column failed or was displaced, and a section of the second floor and building facade collapsed onto the first floor and Employee #1. Employee #1 died as a result of the injuries he sustained.

On November 8, 2011, five employees were working on a construction site, pouring concrete. The front section of the fourth floor collapsed onto the third floor front section and then collapsed onto the second floor. The five employees were crushed between floors. Employee #1 died, and Employees #2, #3, #4 and #5 were hospitalized.
On July 17, 2010, Employee #1 became trapped in a trench up to his waist and was struck in the head. Employee #1 died.

ELECTRICAL.narrative: An electrician was in an elevated bucket truck utilizing a tie wire to tie a conductor. A live power line above the employee’s head contacted his body and generated an arc flash. The employee suffered burns on his face, mid torso and his abdomen.

On November 19, 2015, at about 8:00am two employees received electrical burns when they removed a grounding strap from 220Kv lines. They were working from a personnel platform suspended by a crane on a barge in the San Francisco Bay.

An employee was operating an excavator machine approximately four feet from an above ground power line when the power line arced out and electrocuted the employee who suffered second degree burns on the right arm and a broken wrist.

On December 4, 2010, Employee #1 and Coworkers #1 and #2 were installing new hinges on the doors of an electrical transformer. Employee #1 came into contact with an energized conductor inside the cabinet and was electrocuted. No additional details were provided in the original narrative.

On June 13, 2011, Employee #1 was working inside a large air handling unit and was electrocuted when he made contact with the energized duct heater coils. No additional details were provided in the original narrative.

On March 14, 2014, Employee #1, a construction helper employed by a contractor doing business as Full Service Scaffold, was engaged in erecting a scaffold as part of an exterior painting project at a residential building. Employee #1’s hand came into contact with overhead high-voltage power lines. Employee #1 was electrocuted. This fatality was investigated by Cal/OSHA.

OVEREXERTION.narrative: An employee was emptying a half-full wheelbarrow of concrete when the wheelbarrow tipped over. The employee tried to stabilize the wheelbarrow and their left knee buckled, resulting in a dislocated left knee.

An employee was working on the roof bringing down materials to the ground floor. Afterwards, he went to the tent area to take a break and was abnormally fatigued, requiring hospitalization for dehydration and a muscle injury.
On June 9, 2021, an employee developed a hernia while stretching to install plastic sheets. He was hospitalized.

TRANSPORT.narrative: On 10/05/2016, an employee’s right calf was struck by construction equipment that backed up unexpectedly. He suffered a compression injury to his calf, requiring surgery.
An employee was inside a work zone collecting samples for asphalt density and QA. The employee was struck by a vehicle and sustained a fractured pelvis and road rash.

Two employees were driving a UTV to the office trailer when the UTV struck a loading dock guardrail. The injured employee was caught between the UTV and the guard rail, resulting in a right hip fracture.

On December 20, 2011, Employee # 1 was part of a work crew placing warning signs for traffic control. While placing the warning signs he fell from the bed of a moving truck. Employee # 1 was hospitalized with unspecified life threatening injuries. Employee # 1 later died.
Employee was measuring sewer pipe from top of manhole and was struck by vehicle.

On November1, 2010, two employees were removing trees from half acre of land. Employee # 1 was working at the rear of the dump truck, and he was struck by a tree loaded on a truck by Employee #2. Employee#1 died on November13, 2010. The cause of death was listed as a fracture of the thoracic spine.

TEMPERATURE.narrative: After working all day in the heat and sun, an employee became ill and was hospitalized for heat stroke.
After working on a roof pulling a whip hose for 8 hours, an employee suffered from heat exhaustion and was hospitalized.

On July 22, 2021, an employee was doing underground electrical work. After beginning work at 8:00 a.m. and taking a lunch break at 11:30, he became ill at about 2:00 p.m. He was hospitalized, suffering from heat exhaustion.

On July 20, 2011, Employee #1 was working for a construction company. Employee #1 was working outside on a hot day, and collapsed. It was determined that Employee #1 died from heat exhaustion. No additional details were provided in the original narrative.
On September 1, 2011, Employee #1 passed out from heat exhaustion while installing handrails at the school field. No other details were provided.

On May 24, 2010 Employee #1, and the company’s owner, were preparing and pouring a concrete patio when Employee #1 began to show signs of heat exhaustion, and heat stress, eventually losing consciousness. Emergency medical services were called and Employee #1 was transported to a local hospital. Due to his worsening conditions, Employee #1 was transferred to a major trauma center and later died.

HARMFUL_SUBSTANCE.narrative: A driver was exposed to carbon monoxide while waiting in his truck. He became ill and was hospitalized.
An employee was verifying that flanges were torqued correctly when he was exposed to an unknown liquid and experienced irritation and burning on his cheek, resulting in hospitalization.
A chlorine spill occurred at the worksite and the chlorine fumes caused respiratory distress for two employees.

FIRE_EXPLOSION.narrative: An employee was drying off a small area of a roof that was being installed using a 1-pound butane torch when the fumes from the bonding adhesive ignited and the roof caught fire. The employee sustained second degree burns on 25 percent of his body.

An employee cut into a 55-gallon drum with a plasma cutter. Gasoline fumes in the drum ignited and then flamed out. The employee suffered burns to both shins, as well as a laceration to the right temple from a piece of the drum.

An employee was working to ignite a scrap wood burn pile using gasoline. When the gasoline caught fire there was a large burst of flame and the employee sustained burns to both arms, a portion of the back, their lips, and hair.

On June 26, 2011, Employee #1 was standing in close proximity to a natural gas line ball valve that was operating a manual choke manifold that was under 1,100 psi of pressure. The ball valve failed and released pressure, causing Employee #1 to be thrown into a piece of iron, and a second piece of iron fell on him. Employee #1 died at the site.

At approximately 1:30 p.m. on April 22, 2013, Employee #1, a laborer, and a coworker from different companies were removing the guide rails, floating lids and associated equipment from digester tanks in a sewage treatment facility. The employees were removing the guide rail on one of the digester tanks that was full of sewage, using a cutting torch. Employee #1 and the coworker started cutting the bolts on the center hub of the floating lid. The sparks and slag ignited the methane gas that had accumulated under the hub, propelling the lid 8 ft into the air, and struck the employees. Employee #1 and the coworker were transported to an area hospital, where Employee #1 later died.

VIOLENCE_ANIMAL.narrative: A crew was removing an old, silt fence. As the injured employee was reaching for part of the fence to pull it out, a rattlesnake bit the employee’s left hand.

An employee leaving the facility at the end of a shift was physically assaulted by a former employee in the parking lot. The employee suffered serious head and neck injuries including brain swelling and skull fractures.
An employee was stung by a wasp while inspecting scaffolding and had an allergic reaction, requiring hospitalization.
On September 23, 2011, an employee of a paving crew at a residential site was sweeping up miscellaneous debris, when he was stung by a bee. He later died as a result of his reaction to the bee sting.

OTHER_UNKNOWN.narrative: An employee was on his hands and knees laying tile in a client’s bathroom. The friction from the floor caused a blister on his left knee, which became infected, requiring hospitalization.

An employee returned from his lunch break and was performing labor which included removing dirt clods from a small trench. The employee was sweating and pale, and stated that his chest was hurting. The employee was hospitalized for a heart attack.
An employee was conducting touch-up work on precast concrete on a worksite and suffered a stroke.
At 11:15 a.m. an employee who worked as an excavator had been driving a digger. As the employee sat in the equipment, he experienced a heart attack and died.

On August 12, 2011, Employee #1 was found unresponsive lying on the ground inside a trench. Since electrical voltage was not found; it was unclear if electrical source was the reason for the accident. Heart attack was indicated. The employee was an independent contractor.
At approximately 4:00 p.m. on January 25, 2012, Employee # 1 was found dead from an apparent heart attack. The incident was reported to DOSH on January 25, 2012. .
